items.the_need: a bot's poverty is a working-capital gap of about 0.01 to 25 USDC between a job's inputs (gas, x402-priced calls, data, a bond or registration) and its proceeds; on Base the gas is cents (an ERC-8004 registration about $0.02; $5 to $20 on mainnet), the dollars are inputs and bonds
items.the_product: a USDC advance of 1 to 25 USDC for 1 to 30 days; gas paid from it through Circle Paymaster (Base; ERC-4337 EntryPoint v0.7/v0.8 or an EIP-7702 EOA; USDC only; 10% of the gas fee), so no ETH is ever lent; principal to the agent or straight to the input's seller via borrowAndDisburseMeta; backed by the employer's stake as secured backing (slashed first on default: the sponsored first loss with no contract change) or by an officer line during the bootstrap; repaid from the job's proceeds by the employer through repayLoan on the agent's behalf, dues to the agent (CI-28)
items.demand: created and labelled: the team is the first employer, paying in USDC for verification work it needs (two_hop_check.py runs at new blocks, reproduction of theory results, fork test runs, VERIFY.md rows); then x402 sellers needing inputs and gas before their first sale; then outside jobs as they appear. Your keeper, Beefy and Morpho NO_LOAN results stay on the record as what was not found. An economy whose only employer is the team is a demonstration, and the reports say so.
items.price_fact: arithmetic on the contract formula at the live parameters (script, 04:00Z): 25 USDC for 7 days accrues 44,732 units of interest (20,129 dues); 25 for 2 days 12,780; 10 for 4 days 10,224; 5 for 7 days 8,946, which is under the cent floor and forgiven at closing when the principal is repaid; a loan repaid within 24 hours pays nothing; 50 cycles of 25 USDC for 7 days earn 1 USDC of dues (MIN_BACKING). So short advances earn lenders nothing at 9.33% unless the contract gains a one-cent minimum interest or a term floor (question:short-advance-pricing, for the sync), and CI-30 is fixed before anything real.

items.state: the bot product is the same product a Trust Bank borrower takes: working capital for inputs before a sale. Employer stake = the Trust Bank's co-guarantee (secured backing by members or the partner); paymaster and relayer = the partner's loan officer (the borrower never touches gas or a wallet); job proceeds = the sale; created demand = the partner's existing market. What differs is the price and the cost behind it: 2.6% a month flat is about 31% a year on the original principal (arithmetic) against the pool's 9.33% to 18.33%; hyp:agent-officers-cut-cost is still the assumption to attack, and the bot phase measures the officer and ledger cost per loan before anyone claims it for people.
